macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks finished lower as investors waited for inflation data
items.summary: Major U.S. indexes ended Tuesday modestly in the red, with the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all lower as markets turned cautious ahead of Wednesday’s CPI report. Futures were little changed in early trading, reflecting a wait-and-see tone across equities.

items.title: U.S. labor market weakens sharply with July jobs decline
items.summary: The U.S. economy unexpectedly lost 23,000 jobs in July, while the unemployment rate fell to 4.1% and ADP reported only 44,000 private-sector job gains, signaling a softer labor market. The weak payroll backdrop is being watched closely for implications for the Fed’s next move.

items.title: Markets await U.S. CPI as investors seek clues on Fed policy
items.summary: Markets are focused on July consumer inflation, with economists expecting headline CPI to slow to 3.4% year over year and core inflation to ease to 2.5%. Traders are using the report to gauge whether the Fed may stay on hold or shift toward easing later this year.
items.source: Reuters via Global Banking & Finance / Barchart

items.title: Dollar firms slightly ahead of key inflation readings
items.summary: The dollar index edged higher toward 99.9 as investors positioned for the CPI release and its potential impact on Federal Reserve expectations. Treasury market attention was also centered on a scheduled 10-year note auction and other macro data.

items.title: Oil prices rose and weighed on sentiment amid Middle East tensions
items.summary: U.S. stocks fell in the previous session as oil prices rose on renewed geopolitical concerns, with market participants worried about inflation pressure and the outlook for rates. The move also left equity futures muted as traders awaited more clarity.

items.title: Stock futures were mixed-to-flat ahead of CPI
items.summary: S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures were near unchanged to slightly higher in early Wednesday trade as investors held positions ahead of inflation data. The market backdrop was dominated by rate expectations and oil-driven inflation concerns.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox-owned action-adventure game lands on PlayStation Store
items.summary: A new PlayStation Store release brings one of Xbox’s action-adventure titles to PS5, with the game now available as a digital standard edition. The listing highlights the continued cross-platform expansion of formerly Xbox-exclusive releases.

items.title: Crimson Desert Switch 2 port reported in playable state
items.summary: Nintendo Life reports that the Switch 2 version of Crimson Desert is now playable, with a release target set for the first half of 2027. The update suggests the console port is moving forward in development.

items.title: Genshin Impact 7.0 adds new region and major update in Korea roundup
items.summary: A Korean gaming roundup says Genshin Impact’s 7.0 update is going live, opening the new region of Snezhnaya. The same roundup also highlights several current and upcoming releases, including Akatori and Hell Let Loose: Vietnam.

items.title: Alan Wake 2 crosses 3 million sales
items.summary: Gamereactor reports that Alan Wake 2 has now sold 3 million copies, marking a major commercial milestone for Remedy’s survival-horror sequel. The figure adds to a busy day of industry and sales updates.

items.title: Remedy says Alan Wake 2 has recouped development costs
items.summary: A Chinese-language roundup citing Remedy’s half-year financial update says Alan Wake 2 has surpassed 3 million sales and has now recovered its development budget. The report frames the game as having reached profitability.

items.title: Xbox boss previews Elder Scrolls 6 after private live playthrough
items.summary: PureXbox reports that Xbox boss Asha Sharma shared brief reactions after seeing a behind-closed-doors live playthrough of The Elder Scrolls 6. The comments renewed attention around the long-awaited Bethesda project.

items.title: Steam data breach exposes customer information
items.summary: The Verge reports that a breach involving a Steam hardware shipper may have leaked customer data, including names and addresses. Valve said the information was likely compromised.

items.title: Xbox and PC age verification rollout reported in Australia
items.summary: The Verge also reports that Xbox and PC users in Australia are being notified about upcoming age verification requirements for purchasing 18+ apps and games. The change would affect storefront access for adult-rated content.

items.title: New Quake expansion released for free
items.summary: The Verge notes that Quake has received a new free expansion, adding fresh content to the classic shooter. The update is one of several notable game-release stories highlighted in the past day.

items.title: Minecraft Switch 2 release dated for October
items.summary: The Verge reports that Minecraft is coming to Switch 2 on October 27. The announcement gives one of Nintendo’s key third-party launches a firm release date.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: RTX GPU prices jump 30% overnight
items.summary: Retail pricing for Nvidia RTX graphics cards surged sharply, with the RTX 5070 reportedly reaching $900. The move underscores continued volatility in consumer GPU pricing and supply-demand pressure in the PC hardware market.

items.title: OpenAI brings ChatGPT desktop app to Linux
items.summary: OpenAI released a dedicated ChatGPT desktop app for Linux, expanding the chatbot’s desktop footprint beyond Windows and macOS. The launch is part of a broader push to make ChatGPT more accessible across operating systems.

items.title: Google’s Gemini app reportedly reaches one billion users
items.summary: Google said the Gemini app has grown to one billion users, putting it in the same league as ChatGPT’s reported scale. The milestone signals intensifying competition in mainstream consumer AI chat products.

items.title: Tesla and SpaceX plan $16.8B Texas chip factory investment
items.summary: Tesla and SpaceX are reportedly committing $16.8 billion to begin building a “Terafab” chip factory in Texas. The project highlights rising interest in domestic semiconductor manufacturing capacity tied to advanced hardware needs.

items.title: India’s Yulu raises $93 million
items.summary: Yulu secured $93 million in Series C funding as demand for electric bikes rises alongside the quick-commerce boom. The company plans to expand its EV fleet to 200,000 vehicles.

items.title: Joby Aviation expands defense business with $500 million acquisition
items.summary: Joby Aviation is building out its defense business through a $500 million acquisition. The move suggests the eVTOL company is diversifying beyond passenger aviation into military and government markets.

items.title: Anthropic says it will watermark text generated by its models
items.summary: Anthropic announced plans to watermark text generated by its AI systems, including support for older models. The development comes amid wider scrutiny of provenance and authenticity in machine-generated content.

items.title: OpenAI reports unlimited text chats for free users
items.summary: OpenAI said free and Go users will get unlimited text chats, along with a new “think” button for more complex queries. The change is part of broader product updates aimed at widening usage.
